text:
maria.g: quick heads-up — I ran an nsys sweep on the latest canary (flash-attn+fused kernels, runtime v0.27.1) against the 8k sequence sim workload and saw a ~12% p99 token-latency regression vs main. timeline shows repeated KV-cache write serialization right after attention, looks like small write bursts that stall following kernels. attaching notes and traces below.

maria.g: nsys summary (snip):
```
GPU activities: kernels  85.2%  memory  9.1%  others  5.7%
Top kernels: flash_attn_fused  38%  (many short launches)
kv_cache_write  16%  (lots of tiny writes, serial)
softmax_kernel  8%
```

maria.g: perfetto link: https://perfetto.redwood/traces/1859508762 (nvlink + nsys traces) — timeline shows pattern: flash_attn_fused -> kv_cache_write xN -> blocked GEMM/softmax.

dmitri.v: can you paste the nsys cmd you used? curious about batch shape & the batching heuristic in the runner. if the runtime falls back to small-batch path it can force per-request syncs.

maria.g: cmd: `nsys profile -o /tmp/run1859 --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=none --capture-range=cuda_api_start,cuda_api_stop -- python perf/sim_run.py --model gptx-7b --seq 8192 --batch 2 --profile-mode sim`
observed that when batcher splits request into [1,1] micro-batches the kvcache writes are interleaved with attention kernels.

ashley: saw something similar locally. nvprof flame shows the write kernel has lots of small memcpy-from-host style chunks (not H2D, but small device-to-device memcpy regions) which align with membank conflicts on A100-80GB. on that hardware the fused flash variant allocates tile-aligned buffers differently which increases bank conflicts at wide seq lengths.

ashley: paste from nvprof timeline:
```
0.000s flash_attn_fused (23us)
0.0003s kv_cache_write (15us)
0.00055s flash_attn_fused (20us)
0.00085s kv_cache_write (17us)
... repeated pattern, stalls after 2nd write
```

kevin: any chance kernel-selection heuristic picked fused because peak_scratch < threshold? we added a heuristic to prefer fused when scratch < 256MB, but at high seq lengths the fragmented allocs push working set across multiple memory banks. might need a bank-conflict cost term.

maria.g: I instrumented the heuristic flag and forced non-fused flash variant — regression disappears, latency actually improves ~6% vs main. so this is definitely a selection problem, not model weight mismatch.

perf-bot: automated trace summary: 1859508762 — p99 latency 12% up, top contributors: kv_cache_write (16% time), flash_attn_fused (38% launches, high launch overhead), high kernel enqueue stalls (5.4% rdtsc).

dmitri.v: probably two immediate fixes: 1) add membank-aware scoring term to kernel selector; 2) short-term: relax fused preference for sequences > 4096 or when observed small-write-rate > X. also add a micro-benchmark in perf-suite that runs sequences [2k,4k,8k] on canary and validates choose-kernel decision.

ashley: agree. I'll prototype a bank-conflict heuristic: sample device SASS metrics for memory warp divergence and estimate conflict score. cheap to compute during model load.

kevin: I'll open a revert PR to force non-fused on the rollout channel so we stop impacting prod experiments while we root-cause. followup PR will add selector change + perf test.

maria.g: action items:
- kevin: revert canary selection to non-fused for rollout (PR by EOD)
- ashley: prototype membank heuristic & perf patch (WIP, aim for tomorrow)
- dmitri: add micro-benchmark to perf-suite and a watchdog assertion for kernel selection (low-risk)
- perf-bot: attach traces to the new perf job and alert on >5% p99 regression vs main

maria.g: posting this here in case runtime/serving folks want to look at traces. cc @dmitri.v @ashley @kevin :thumbsup:

kevin: ack, starting revert now. will ping when PR is up.

ashley: quick note — I also saw a minor write-amplification when KV entries are sharded across 4 banks; profiling shows coalesced writes would be much faster. will add that to the prototype.

maria.g: thanks — if anyone wants the raw nsys .qdrep I left it on /shared/perf/1859508762.qdrep.
